liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugar Magnolia** (2 reviews): The opening line of Sugar Magnolia is sung by Jerry, according to the reviewer, who had long doubted it with a friend [13][14]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): The jam in Looks Like Rain has a sound like a theremin being played [9]
- **El Paso** (1 review): Archive.org and setlists.net omit El Paso, yet it appears in this recording [8]
- **Casey Jones** (1 other source): The first few seconds of Casey Jones are missing from this recording [1]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Keith's playing in the Truckin' jam is full of energy [11]
- **Weather Report Suite** (1 review): Weather Report Suite and Let It Grow feel like a funky improvised jazz session [15]

## Setlist highlights

- **Tico Tico**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 7 archived performances [17]
- **Let Me Sing Your Blues Away**: rare: 8 archived performances [17]
- **Vaudeville Chorus Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-09-17.150977.sbd.patched.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 172 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1973-09-17.sbd.jensen.10082.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 180 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1973-09-17.sbd.sirmick.107542.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 166 min; rated 4.5/5 by 14 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the recording's sound quality [16]
- **gd73-09-17.sbd.cotsman.14473.d3fixed.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 163 min; rated 4/5 by 14 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound quality good [9]

## Around the show

- Horns joined the band in the second set as Wake of the Flood material began, which was unexpected [5]
- Horn player Martin Fierro came from Doug Sahm's band, which opened this show [6]
- Reviewer says the sound inside the hall was terrible, though the second set was very different and excellent [7]
- Martin Fierro gets room to stretch out on horn during this show [16]
- Most of set two features Joe Ellis on trumpet and Martin Fierro on saxophone [1]
- Martin Fierro and Joe Ellis play horns on the starred songs [2]
- Doug Sahm opened the show [3]
- Martin Fierro and Joe Ellis play horns from Let Me Sing Your Blues Away through Sugar Magnolia, except Truckin' and Stella Blue [3]
- Reviewer saw other 1973 shows but found this one unique [5]
- Fierro also played on the Wake of the Flood LP and with Jerry's band alongside Merle Saunders [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-09-17.150977.sbd.patched.miller.flac1644**: taped by Rob Eaton and Dick Latvala; transferred by Original Transfer and Mastering by Rob Eaton Additional Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 30, 2020; source: SBD > Reel Master (7in 7.5ips 1/2trk) > DAT (Panasonic SV-3700/44.1k) > DAT (Panasonic SV-3700/44.1k) [1]. Also: Patched from two sources supplied by Rob Eaton and Dick Latvala; most first-set tunings have an added cassette generation [1]
- **gd1973-09-17.sbd.jensen.10082.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Tyler Jensen; source: MSR>C>DAT>DAT [2]. Also: Taken from a DAT with no editing except removing about 7.65 seconds of noise at 39:54 [2]
- **gd1973-09-17.sbd.sirmick.107542.flac16**: transferred by SIRMick; source: SBD > Master Reel [3]
- **gd73-09-17.sbd.cotsman.14473.d3fixed.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
